title: Topic Drill: Revising Essays: Organization, Transitions, Cohesion and Style (Set B)

items.stem:
______ (1) The turbine sits twenty meters below the surface and turns slowly as the tide moves in and out. (2) Unlike wind, tides arrive on a schedule printed years ahead, so engineers can predict the output hour by hour. (3) The machine sits beside the boat channel instead of across it, so ferries and fishing boats pass freely.

Which sentence would be the best introduction for this paragraph?
options: A small tidal turbine in Marlow Harbor offers a predictable and boat friendly way to make electricity.
Tides rise and fall twice each day in most coastal towns around the world.
Electricity is used in homes, schools, and businesses every day of the year.
The Marlow Harbor turbine cost more than the first estimate suggested, which surprised several town officials.
items.explanation: The body describes the turbine’s depth, its predictable output, and its safe placement beside the channel, so the best introduction names those ideas. The tide statement is true but never leads to the turbine. The electricity sentence is far too broad. The cost claim introduces a topic the paragraph never discusses.

items.stem:
(1) Next, crews lowered the turbine to the seabed with a crane barge. (2) Before anything went into the water, divers surveyed the seabed for rocks and cables. (3) Finally, engineers connected the cable to the shore station and tested the output. (4) The Marlow Harbor pilot was installed in three stages.

Which order of sentences makes this paragraph most logical?
items.explanation: The paragraph should open with the general claim about three stages, then follow the clues in time order: the survey happens before anything enters the water, the lowering comes next, and the connection and test come finally. Starting with the survey buries the main idea. Lowering before surveying reverses the real sequence. Testing before lowering is impossible.

items.stem:
(1) The Marlow Harbor tidal pilot began in March with one turbine and a small monitoring shed. (2) Local students visit monthly to read the gauges and log the power output. (3) Their charts show the output rising and falling in a steady rhythm tied to the moon. (4) The project also has a budget story. (5) Grant money covered the first two years, and the town council must now decide how to fund a third. (6) Council members will hear a cost report in January.

At which sentence should a new paragraph begin?
options: Sentence 2, because the students who visit are a completely new subject for the paragraph.
Sentence 3, because charts always need a paragraph of their own.
Sentence 4, because the writer turns from how the pilot operates to how it is paid for.
Sentence 6, because a date should open a new paragraph.
items.explanation: Sentences 1 through 3 describe the pilot’s equipment and monitoring, and sentence 4 announces a different topic, funding. A break there separates two unified ideas. Students and their charts still belong to the monitoring description. Sentence 6 only adds one detail to the funding discussion, so a break there would leave a one line paragraph.

items.stem:
(1) A camera near the turbine tracks fish in the harbor. (2) The harbor biologist reviews the footage every week. (3) The blades turn slowly and at a gentle speed, which makes it easy for fish to swim past safely without harm. (4) So far, no injuries have been recorded.

Which is the best revision of sentence 3 to remove redundancy?
options: The blades turn slowly at a gentle pace, so fish can swim past safely and without harm.
Fish swim past the blades, which turn slowly, gently, and at a slow speed.
The blades turn at a gentle speed, which fish find it easy to swim past safely without harm.
The blades turn at a gentle speed, which lets fish swim past safely.
items.explanation: Slowly and at a gentle speed say the same thing, as do safely and without harm. The key keeps one phrase for each idea and stays grammatical. The second choice still repeats slowly and gentle pace, and safely with without harm. The third stacks slowly, gently, and slow speed. The last choice is also ungrammatical.

items.stem:
(1) The Alder Street seed library opened in a retired card catalog holding sixty envelopes of beans, tomatoes, and herbs. (2) Members borrow a packet in spring and promise to return seeds from their best plants in fall. (3) No one is charged a fee or asked for a deposit.

______, the library’s value goes beyond free seeds. (5) Neighbors swap growing tips at the monthly meeting, and new gardeners find mentors there.

Which transition best fills the blank to connect the two paragraphs?
options: In addition
Therefore
Otherwise
In contrast
items.explanation: The second paragraph adds a further benefit to the borrowing system described in the first, so an additive transition fits. Therefore would claim the meetings result from the free packets. Otherwise would set up an unstated condition. In contrast would signal an opposition, but the two paragraphs both praise the library.

items.stem:
(1) The Alder Street seed library should extend its hours to include weekends. (2) Right now it opens only on weekday afternoons, when most gardeners are at work. (3) Longer hours would bring in more borrowers and more returned seeds.

Which sentence would best add evidence to support sentence 1?
options: Weekend hours would be wonderful for everyone who loves to garden, grow vegetables, and share seeds with neighbors.
Last month, 14 of the 22 people who asked about borrowing seeds said they could visit only on Saturday.
The oak card catalog that holds the seeds was built in the 1950s.
Seeds are tiny, and they come in many different shapes and colors.
items.explanation: A claim about hours needs concrete evidence about visitors and their schedules, and the count of people who could visit only on Saturday supplies it. The first distractor repeats the opinion without proof. The card catalog’s age is an off topic detail. The seed shapes sentence has no link to opening hours.

items.stem:
(1) Our seed library should add a shelf of native wildflower seeds. (2) Native plants feed the bees and butterflies that also pollinate the vegetable beds nearby. (3) Once established, they need less watering, which saves members time and money. (4) ______ (5) For these reasons, the library should add the shelf this spring.

Which sentence, placed at the blank, would best complete the argument of this letter to the editor?
options: Wildflowers come in yellow, purple, white, orange, and many other bright colors that look lovely in a garden bed in summer.
The seed library opened three years ago in a retired card catalog.
Some members worry that wildflowers will crowd out vegetables, but the seeds can be sown in a separate border.
Many people enjoy spending time in the garden each spring.
items.explanation: A strong argument deals with a likely objection before it ends. The remark about crowding names a real worry and offers a solution, so the final recommendation follows naturally. The color detail adds no support. The opening history is off topic. The statement about enjoying the garden is too general to move the case forward.

items.stem:
(1) Welcome to the Alder Street Seed Library! (2) Members are required to return seeds at the end of the growing season in accordance with library policy. (3) You can browse the envelopes any time the library is open.

The handout is a friendly welcome for new neighbors. Which is the best revision of sentence 2 to match that tone?
options: Failure to return seeds when the season ends will be treated as a violation of policy.
When fall comes, we hope you will save a few seeds from your best plants and bring them back to share.
Seeds shall be returned by members upon the termination of the growing season.
Just bring some seeds back whenever, it is no big deal at all, so do not stress.
items.explanation: The welcome handout should sound warm while still telling members what to do. The key invites a return in a neighborly way and keeps the fall deadline. The first distractor sounds like a threat. The second is stiff and legal. The last is so casual that it drops the season and the request, so readers lose the actual instruction.

items.stem:
(1) The Ridgeline Rescue volunteers answer about sixty calls a year. (2) Most involve hikers with sprained ankles or people who lost the trail at dusk. (3) Members train every second Saturday in knots, first aid, and night navigation. (4) Each volunteer also carries a pack with water, a headlamp, and a radio.

Which sentence would best conclude this article?
options: To wrap up, this article has told you about the Ridgeline Rescue volunteers and the many kinds of work that they do for hikers every year.
Some hikers also enjoy camping near the lake during the summer months.
A radio is a device that sends and receives signals through the air.
With steady training and ready packs, the volunteers turn a frightening night on the mountain into a safe trip home.
items.explanation: A good conclusion pulls together the article’s points, here the calls, the training, and the packs, and leaves a final impression. The key does that. The announcement that the article is over adds nothing. The camping sentence starts a new topic. The definition of a radio is an irrelevant detail.

items.stem:
(1) After the call came in, Dana told Priya she should bring the first aid kit. (2) The kit was in the truck, and the truck was parked behind the station. (3) Both volunteers left within two minutes.

Which is the best revision of sentence 1 to fix the unclear pronoun?
options: After the call came in, Dana told Priya to bring the first aid kit.
After the call came in, Dana told Priya that she should bring the first aid kit with her.
After the call came in, Dana told Priya she would bring it.
After the call came in, Dana told Priya that the first aid kit should be brought by her.
items.explanation: In the original, she could mean Dana or Priya. The key removes the pronoun by using an infinitive, so Priya is clearly the one who brings the kit. The other choices keep an ambiguous she or her, and the second also replaces the kit with the vague word it.

items.stem:
(1) If you become separated from your group, stay where you are. (2) Blow your whistle in three short bursts every few minutes. (3) A hiker should also put on an extra layer, because they lose heat quickly when standing still. (4) Rescuers will find you faster if you remain in one place.

Which is the best revision of sentence 3 to fix the shift in point of view?
options: You should also put on an extra layer, because a hiker loses heat quickly when standing still.
A hiker should also put on an extra layer, because you lose heat quickly when standing still.
One should also put on an extra layer, because people lose heat quickly when standing still.
Also put on an extra layer, because you lose heat quickly when standing still.
items.explanation: The safety handout speaks directly to the reader with you, so sentence 3 should keep that voice. The key does so in both clauses. The other choices shift to a hiker, one, or people, or mix a hiker with you, which breaks the handout’s consistent second person voice.

items.stem:
(1) Applicants for the Ridgeline Rescue team must meet three requirements. (2) They must hike six miles with a twenty pound pack, reading a topographic map, and to finish a first aid course. (3) The team reviews applications each January.

Which is the best revision of sentence 2 to make the list parallel?
options: They must hike six miles with a twenty pound pack, reading a topographic map, and finish a first aid course.
They must hiking six miles with a twenty pound pack, to read a topographic map, and finishing a first aid course.
They must hike six miles with a twenty pound pack, read a topographic map, and finish a first aid course.
They must hike six miles with a twenty pound pack, be able to read a map, and the finishing of a first aid course.
items.explanation: Three requirements joined by and need the same grammatical form, and here each should be a base verb phrase after must: hike, read, finish. The key does this. The others mix in reading, to read, finishing, or a noun phrase, so the items no longer match.

items.stem:
______ (1) The Riverbend Community Orchestra rehearses on Monday evenings in the library annex. (2) Its players range from a fourteen year old cellist to a retired mail carrier who plays trumpet. (3) Concerts are free, and the audience often includes neighbors who have never heard live music before.

Which sentence would be the best introduction for this paragraph?
options: The Riverbend Orchestra welcomes players of every age and offers neighbors free concerts.
Music has been performed by orchestras across Europe for hundreds of years.
The library annex has room for about forty chairs, a small stage, and a storage closet for the instruments.
Every orchestra needs a conductor who can keep a steady beat for the players.
items.explanation: The paragraph covers who plays in the orchestra and who can attend, and the key states exactly that. The history of European orchestras is too distant. The annex seating and the conductor sentence are details that the paragraph does not develop, so neither introduces its main idea.

items.stem:
(1) Please bring your own music stand and a pencil. (2) Thank you for joining the Riverbend Community Orchestra this fall. (3) Our first rehearsal is Monday, September 9, at 7 p.m. in the library annex. (4) Rehearsals last two hours, with a short break in the middle.

Which order of sentences would make this welcome email most logical?
items.explanation: A welcome email should open with the thanks, then give the date and place, then the length of rehearsals, and finally what to bring. The key follows that flow. Starting with the date skips the greeting. Putting the stand request before the date asks for things before saying when. Placing it between two rehearsal details splits them apart.

items.stem:
(1) The winter rehearsals begin January 6 and continue every Monday until the concert on February 24. (2) Please arrive by 6:45 so we can tune together. (3) We also need volunteers for concert night. (4) Two people are needed to greet guests, and three to move chairs after the final piece. (5) Reply by January 3 to sign up.

The writer wants to divide this email into two paragraphs. Where should the second paragraph begin?
options: Sentence 2, because arrival time is a new topic.
Sentence 4, because the number of volunteers should stand alone.
Sentence 5, because instructions to reply always form a separate paragraph.
Sentence 3, because the email turns from rehearsals to a request for volunteers.
items.explanation: Sentences 1 and 2 cover the rehearsal schedule, and sentence 3 introduces a separate request for help, so the break belongs there. Arrival time is part of the schedule. Sentence 4 gives the details of the volunteer request, and sentence 5 tells how to answer that same request, so splitting there would cut the request apart.

items.stem:
(1) The orchestra’s last three concerts sold out within a week. (2) A waiting list of sixty names now grows before every performance.

______ (4) The annex seats only 120, and standing listeners crowd the hallway. (5) The board is touring two larger halls this month.

Which sentence, placed at the blank, would best begin the second paragraph and link it to the first?
options: Orchestras have performed in many kinds of halls throughout history.
That growing demand has created a problem of space.
Tickets are sold at the library desk and on the orchestra’s website, and they cost eight dollars each.
The conductor will lead a new piece by a local composer next spring.
items.explanation: The first paragraph shows rising demand, and the second discusses crowding and a search for larger halls, so the opening sentence should connect demand to the space problem. The history of halls is too broad. Ticket sales and the new composition are true details but they do not bridge the two paragraphs.

items.stem:
(1) The Greenlane Food Co-op keeps a wall of bulk bins for grains, beans, and dried fruit. (2) Due to the fact that members buy only what they need, they waste less food at home, and the reason for this is that there is no fixed package size.

Which is the best revision of sentence 2 to make it more concise?
options: Because of the fact that members buy only what they need, less food is wasted by them at home.
Members, who buy only what they need, waste less food at home, and the reason is that no fixed package size exists.
Members buy only what they need and so they do not waste as much food at home, which is a good thing.
Members buy only what they need, so they waste less food at home.
items.explanation: The original piles up filler such as due to the fact that and the reason for this is that. The key keeps the cause and the result in one short clause. The other choices keep the filler, switch to a passive structure, or add the empty comment that wasting less is a good thing.

items.stem:
(1) The co-op’s new weekly produce box has been a success. (2) ______ (3) Based on these numbers, the board plans to offer the box all year.

Which sentence would best fill the blank to support sentence 1 with evidence?
options: Everyone at the co-op seems to love getting fresh vegetables each week.
Produce boxes have been used by farms in many countries for decades.
Sign ups rose from 18 households in March to 64 in June, and only three families dropped out.
The boxes are packed on Thursday mornings in the back room.
items.explanation: Sentence 3 refers to these numbers, so the missing sentence must contain figures that show success, and the growth from 18 to 64 households with few dropouts does that. The first choice is a vague opinion. The history of produce boxes is off topic. The packing schedule has no numbers and does not show success.

items.stem:
(1) The Greenlane Food Co-op should accept payment cards at its farm stand. (2) Many shoppers no longer carry cash. (3) Last Saturday I watched three people leave without buying fresh corn because the stand took only cash. (4) ______ (5) Accepting cards would help both shoppers and the farmers.

Which sentence, placed at the blank, would best complete the argument of this letter to the editor?
options: Corn tastes best when it is picked in the morning and eaten that night.
Each lost sale means less income for the farmers the co-op was created to support.
The farm stand sits in the parking area beside the front door.
The co-op has been open since 2012 and now has two hundred members.
items.explanation: Sentence 5 says cards would help the farmers, so sentence 4 must connect the lost corn sales to the farmers’ income. The key makes that link. The corn flavor, the stand’s location, and the co-op’s history are accurate details but none of them support the claim about helping farmers.

items.stem:
(1) Hey board, the walk in cooler is acting up again and it is super annoying. (2) It has been above 40 degrees twice this week, so we might lose a bunch of dairy. (3) Can someone please call the repair guy as soon as possible?

This memo will go to the co-op’s board of directors. Which is the best revision of sentence 1 for a formal workplace memo?
options: The walk in cooler has again failed to hold its temperature, and a repair is needed this week.
Dear respected members of the esteemed board, it is with the deepest regret that I must humbly report a cooler problem.
The cooler is totally broken again, which is really annoying, so please deal with it.
Repairs to the walk in cooler are being considered, so the board might possibly wish to look into them.
items.explanation: A formal memo states the problem plainly and professionally, and the key names the failure and the need for action. The first distractor is overblown and wordy. The second keeps the casual, irritated tone. The third is so vague and hedged that it hides the urgency the later sentences describe.

items.stem:
(1) The Late Line night bus runs from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. (2) It stops at the hospital, the library, and the train station. (3) Riders who work late shifts say the bus is very helpful and useful, and they find it helpful because it gets them home.

Which is the best revision of sentence 3 to remove redundancy?
options: Riders who work late shifts say the bus is helpful and useful, and it gets them home safely.
Riders who work late shifts say the bus is useful, helpful, and a service that helps them get home.
Riders who work late shifts, riders who finish work late, say the bus gets them home.
Riders who work late shifts say the bus is useful because it gets them home.
items.explanation: Helpful and useful are near synonyms, and the original repeats helpful a third time. The key uses one adjective and keeps the reason. The other choices still pair helpful with useful, add a third form of help, or repeat the idea of riders who work late within the same sentence.

items.stem:
(1) The night bus starts at the depot. (2) It goes to the hospital. (3) It goes to the library. (4) It ends at the train station.

Which is the best way to combine these sentences to vary the rhythm and avoid wordiness?
options: Starting at the depot, the night bus stops at the hospital and the library before ending at the train station.
The night bus starts at the depot, and it goes to the hospital, and it goes to the library, and it ends at the train station.
The night bus starts at the depot, going to the hospital, going to the library, ends at the train station.
The night bus starts at the depot, it goes to the hospital and the library, it ends at the train station.
items.explanation: The key joins four choppy sentences into one smooth sentence with a varied opening and a clear order of stops. The first distractor strings clauses with and, which stays wordy. The second mixes participles and a finite verb. The third links three independent clauses with commas only, a comma splice.

items.stem:
(1) Drivers turn in umbrellas and bags that riders leave on the bus to the depot staff. (2) They keep them in a locked closet for thirty days.

Which is the best revision of sentence 2 to fix the unclear pronouns?
options: They store the umbrellas and bags in a locked closet for thirty days.
The depot staff keep the items in a locked closet for thirty days.
Then the items are kept by them in a locked closet for thirty days.
The ones kept in a locked closet stay there for thirty days by them.
items.explanation: In sentence 2, They could mean the drivers or the staff, and them could mean the riders or the items. The key names the staff and the items, so nothing is unclear. The first and second distractors keep a vague they, and the last adds an awkward by them with no clear referent.

items.stem:
(1) The Late Line night bus gives people who work late a safe way home. (2) Last month it carried 1,400 riders, many of them nurses and kitchen staff. (3) The city plans to cut the route in July to save money. (4) Each canceled ride means someone must find another way home at midnight.

Which sentence would best conclude this letter to the editor?
options: That is all I have to say about the Late Line for now.
Buses have been used for public transportation in cities and towns all around the world since the middle of the nineteenth century.
The council should keep the Late Line running, because the savings are small and the cost to workers is large.
Some riders prefer window seats because they can watch the streets go by.
items.explanation: A persuasive letter should end with a clear call to action grounded in its reasons, and the key asks the council to keep the route and weighs savings against harm. The first distractor only signals the end. The history of buses and the window seat preference drift away from the argument.

items.stem:
______ (1) At the Hollin Road Repair Cafe, volunteers fix toasters, lamps, torn jackets, and wobbly chairs while the owners watch. (2) Owners learn basic skills such as soldering a cord or sewing a seam. (3) Items that would have gone to the landfill stay in use for years.

Which sentence would be the best introduction for this paragraph?
options: The cafe meets in the church hall on the first Sunday of each month from noon to four o’clock.
The Hollin Road Repair Cafe saves items from the landfill and teaches neighbors to fix them.
Toasters were first sold to the public in the early part of the last century.
Throwing things away is a habit that most people find hard to break.
items.explanation: The body shows two results, fewer discarded items and new skills for owners, and the key names both. The meeting schedule is a detail the paragraph does not use. The toaster history is off topic. The statement about throwing things away is general and never mentions the cafe’s work.

items.stem:
(1) Then a volunteer will look at the item with you and explain what went wrong. (2) Start by filling out a repair card at the front desk with your name and a description of the problem. (3) If the repair is finished, take your item home; if parts are needed, the volunteer will note them on your card. (4) Wait in the seating area until a volunteer calls your name.

Which order of sentences makes this handout most logical?
items.explanation: A how to handout follows the order of the visitor’s actions: fill out the card, wait to be called, work with the volunteer, then finish or note the parts needed. The word Then in sentence 1 shows it follows the waiting. Waiting before filling out the card, meeting the volunteer before being called, or finishing before the diagnosis breaks the sequence.

items.stem:
(1) When I first came to the repair cafe, I brought a broken lamp. (2) A volunteer showed me how to test the cord. (3) You learn quickly when someone patient guides you. (4) By the end of the hour, I had fixed the lamp myself.

Which is the best revision of sentence 3 to fix the shift in point of view?
options: I learned quickly because someone patient guided me.
We learn quickly when someone patient guides us.
One learns quickly when someone patient guides them.
You learned quickly when a patient volunteer guided you.
items.explanation: The anecdote is told in the first person with I and me, so sentence 3 should stay there. The key keeps that voice and the past tense of the story. The other choices switch to we, one, or you, which changes the speaker partway through the account.

items.stem:
(1) Volunteers at the cafe are known for their patience, their skill, and being generous with their time. (2) One retired electrician has repaired more than two hundred lamps. (3) A tailor mends coats at the sewing table.

Which is the best revision of sentence 1 to make the series parallel?
options: Volunteers at the cafe are known for being patient, their skill, and their generosity with time.
Volunteers at the cafe are known for their patience, being skilled, and generosity with time.
Volunteers at the cafe are known for patience, for their skill, and for being generous with their time.
Volunteers at the cafe are known for their patience, their skill, and their generosity with time.
items.explanation: The three items should all be the same kind of phrase. The key uses three noun phrases that begin with their: patience, skill, generosity. The other choices mix a being phrase with noun phrases or change the pattern halfway, so the items do not match.

items.stem:
(1) The Westbrook radio club teaches students more than how to use a microphone. (2) ______ (3) Skills like these also help in classrooms and in future jobs.

Which sentence would best fill the blank to support sentence 1 with an example?
options: The club’s microphone was donated by an electronics store in town.
Radio waves travel through the air at the speed of light, and they can carry both sound and pictures across very long distances.
A student who writes a three minute interview script learns to organize questions and to listen closely to the answers.
Many students enjoy music, sports, art, and clubs of all kinds.
items.explanation: Sentence 3 says skills like these, so the blank needs a concrete example of a skill learned, and the interview script shows organizing and listening. The donated microphone and the radio wave fact are off topic. The sentence about activities students enjoy is general and names no skill.

items.stem:
(1) The Westbrook radio club airs a show every Friday at lunch. (2) Last fall only five students listened.

______ the club began posting the show online and handing out flyers. (4) Within two months the audience grew to eighty.

Which transition best fills the blank to connect the two paragraphs?
options: To change that,
For instance,
Similarly,
Otherwise,
items.explanation: The first paragraph ends with a problem, a tiny audience, and the second describes steps taken to solve it, so a transition showing purpose fits. For instance would promise an example of the five listeners. Similarly would claim the two ideas are alike. Otherwise would suggest an unstated alternative.

items.stem:
(1) Every Friday show opens with a two minute weather report written by a sixth grader. (2) A song from the request box comes next. (3) The interview of the week follows, usually with a teacher or a coach. (4) The host signs off by reading the lunch menu. (5) Behind the scenes, planning for each show starts the Monday before. (6) Writers draft scripts on Tuesday, and hosts rehearse on Wednesday.

The writer wants to divide this excerpt into two paragraphs. Which sentence should begin the second one?
options: Sentence 2, because a song is a different kind of content from a weather report.
Sentence 4, because signing off is the most important part of a show.
Sentence 6, because days of the week should always start a new paragraph.
Sentence 5, because the focus moves from what happens on air to how the show is prepared.
items.explanation: Sentences 1 through 4 follow the show in broadcast order, and sentence 5 starts a different topic, the planning that happens before air time. Sentence 2 still describes the show’s segments. Sentence 4 ends the on air description. Sentence 6 gives details of the planning that sentence 5 introduces, so it belongs with it.

items.stem:
(1) New hosts should read the script aloud once before airing. (2) You gotta hold the mic like, super close to your face, okay? (3) Watch the green light, which tells you when the show is live.

This handout gives clear instructions to new student hosts. Which is the best revision of sentence 2 for that purpose?
options: Experienced hosts generally believe that holding a microphone near the mouth is probably advisable.
Hold the microphone about two inches from your mouth and speak at a steady pace.
Hold the mic super close, like, you know, close enough, and just talk normal.
Some hosts hold the microphone close, while other hosts hold it farther away, depending on taste.
items.explanation: An instructional handout needs a direct command with a clear measure, and the key supplies both. The first distractor hedges and never tells the reader what to do. The second keeps the slangy, vague tone. The third describes habits instead of giving an instruction that a new host could follow right away.

items.stem:
(1) The Fenwick Town Archive plans to scan its collection of old photographs. (2) Many of the prints are fading, and some have cracked. (3) ______ (4) For this reason, the archive is asking residents to help pay for a high quality scanner.

Which sentence would best fill the blank?
options: Without scans, the only copy of each photograph could be lost to a single flood or fire.
The archive’s reading room has oak tables and soft lighting.
Photographs have been popular in family albums since the nineteenth century.
A scanner is a machine that copies pictures and documents into digital files that can be stored on a computer.
items.explanation: Sentence 4 begins with for this reason, so the missing sentence must state the reason scanning is urgent, and the risk of losing the only copy gives it. The reading room description is off topic. The popularity of photographs is true but gives no reason for scanning now. The scanner definition explains a term but not why the plan matters.

items.stem:
(1) The archive holds the minutes of the town council going back to 1902. (2) The minutes of the council meetings date from 1902 to the present day. (3) Visitors may read them on request.

Which is the best way to combine sentences 1 and 2 to remove redundancy?
options: The archive holds the minutes of the town council going back to 1902, and the minutes of council meetings date from 1902.
The archive holds the town council’s minutes from 1902 to the present day.
The archive holds the council minutes from 1902, which date from 1902 to now.
The archive holds the town council’s minutes, which are old, and which are very old minutes.
items.explanation: Both original sentences say that the council minutes start in 1902, so the date and the subject repeat. The key states the subject once and gives the full time span. The first distractor keeps both statements, and the second repeats 1902. The third adds a new redundancy with old and very old.

items.stem:
(1) Each Thursday, archivist Lena Ortiz opens the Fenwick Town Archive to anyone with a question. (2) Last week a resident found his grandfather’s name on a 1931 school roll. (3) A student traced the history of her street through three old maps.

Which sentence would best conclude this profile?
options: The archive is open on Thursday and closed on all the other days of the week.
Maps have been drawn by many cultures using many different materials.
For these visitors, the archive turns names and maps into stories about home.
In summary, the archive is a place that people can visit if they want to.
items.explanation: A concluding sentence should gather the examples, a school roll and old maps, into one idea about the archive’s value. The key does that well. The opening hours restate a detail from the first sentence. The map history drifts away from the archive. The last choice announces a summary but says nothing meaningful.

items.stem:
(1) Archivist Ortiz asked the volunteers to wear gloves, and the council voted to limit each visit to thirty minutes. (2) This protects the old paper, but some visitors find it strict.

Which is the best revision of sentence 2 to fix the unclear reference?
options: This protects the old paper, though some of the visitors who come to read the ledgers find that it is strict.
That protects the old paper, though some visitors find this strict.
This protection of the old paper is a thing that some visitors find strict.
Together, the gloves and the time limit protect the old paper, though some visitors find them strict.
items.explanation: In the original, This and it could point to the gloves, the time limit, or both. The key names both rules and uses the plural them, so the reference is clear. The other choices keep vague words such as this and that, or replace them with a wordy phrase that still does not say what is strict.

items.stem:
______ (1) Visitors ride a shuttle to the base of Turbine 7 and look up at blades longer than the wings of a jumbo jet. (2) A guide explains how the top of the tower turns to face the wind and how the power travels to the substation. (3) In the control room, guests watch the day’s output on a large screen.

Which sentence would be the best introduction for this paragraph?
options: People have used wind to sail ships and grind grain for thousands of years.
The Cedar Flats wind farm tour lets visitors see up close how wind becomes electricity.
The tour ends in a gift shop that sells postcards and small model turbines.
Turbine blades are made from light materials that resist cracking in cold weather.
items.explanation: The paragraph follows a tour that shows the machinery and the control room, so the best introduction names the tour and what visitors learn. The wind history is too distant. The gift shop belongs at the end of the tour and is not discussed. The blade materials are a technical detail that the paragraph never explains.

items.stem:
(1) The Cedar Flats wind farm tour is this Saturday. (2) It lasts two hours and starts at the visitor center. (3) Some people may attend the tour if they wish to do so.

This is a flyer meant to persuade townspeople to sign up. Which is the best revision of sentence 3?
options: Join us on Saturday to stand beneath a turbine and see how your town’s power is made!
Attendance at the tour is permitted for individuals who wish to attend.
You could come, or not, since it does not much matter either way.
The tour will happen, and people will probably be there at some point.
items.explanation: A persuasive flyer should invite readers directly and give them a reason to come, and the key does both with a vivid image. The first distractor is stiff and gives no reason. The second tells readers that attending does not matter. The third is vague and unenthusiastic, so it fails the purpose.

items.stem:
(1) The turbines turn when the wind reaches eight miles an hour. (2) The turbines stop when the wind passes fifty miles an hour. (3) The turbines are stopped to protect the blades from damage.

Which revision best combines these sentences to vary the sentence structure and avoid repetition?
options: The turbines turn when the wind reaches eight miles an hour, and the turbines stop when the wind passes fifty miles an hour, and the turbines are stopped to protect the blades from damage.
Turning at eight miles an hour, the wind stops the turbines at fifty miles an hour to protect the blades.
The turbines turn when the wind reaches eight miles an hour, but they stop above fifty to protect the blades from damage.
The turbines turn when the wind reaches eight miles an hour, the turbines stop above fifty, protecting the blades from damage during very strong storms.
items.explanation: The key joins the three ideas with a contrast and a purpose phrase, and it replaces the repeated subject with they. The first distractor repeats turbines three times. The second has a dangling modifier that makes the wind do the turning. The third joins two independent clauses with only a comma.

items.stem:
(1) That steady supply is now part of the local power grid. (2) The Cedar Flats wind farm began producing electricity in 2021. (3) Within a year its twenty turbines were supplying about six thousand homes. (4) Nearby farmers lease the land under the turbines and keep growing crops around them.

Which order of sentences makes this paragraph most logical?
items.explanation: The paragraph should start with when the farm began, then say how many homes it supplied, and then use that steady supply as the antecedent for sentence 1, ending with the farmers. Putting sentence 1 right after sentence 2 leaves that steady supply without a referent. Starting with sentence 3 comes before the start date. Moving sentence 4 earlier separates the supply from the phrase that refers to it.
